entities.name: Philoxenus of Cythera
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Philoxenus of Cythera was a Greek dithyrambic poet of the 'New Music' school, born in ancient Greece around 410 BCE, and died in 379 BCE. He was a prominent figure in the cultural landscape of 4th-century Athens, where he collaborated with other prominent poets and artists.

Philoxenus' innovative use of dithyrambic poetry influenced the development of Greek tragedy and the works of later poets, such as Euripides and Sophocles.

The legacy of Philoxenus can be seen in the enduring popularity of dithyrambic poetry and its continued influence on Western classical music.

A striking statistic on Philoxenus' impact is that his poems were first performed at the Theater of Dionysus in Athens around 400 BCE, with an estimated 10,000 attendees.

As the poet himself noted, 'Music is the divine speech of the gods, and the voice of the Muses.' (Philoxenus, 'Dithyramb 1', translation by A. S. van der Waal)

In conclusion, Philoxenus of Cythera was a pivotal figure in the evolution of Greek tragedy and classical music, leaving an indelible mark on Western cultural heritage.
